options: Giving credit makes copying a whole copyrighted work legal.
Data protection means keeping personal and sensitive data safe from misuse.
Copyright exists automatically once a work is created.
Using copyrighted material without permission is copyright infringement.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about open source software, cyber crimes and cyber laws:
I. Using strong passwords and two-factor authentication reduces the risk of hacking.
II. Free software always means software with no cost and no source code.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: Free refers to freedom to use, study, modify and share the source code.

items.stem: In the study of e-waste management and health concerns, the term '3R principle' refers to:
items.answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle, the basic approach to managing waste including e-waste
items.markingKey: (c) '3R principle' means reduce, reuse and recycle, the basic approach to managing waste including e-waste.
options: A person who posts provocative or offensive comments online to upset others
The trail of data that a person leaves behind while using the Internet
Reduce, reuse and recycle, the basic approach to managing waste including e-waste
A licensing method that requires modified versions to be shared under the same free terms

items.stem: The following statement about digital footprints and etiquettes is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Replying angrily to trolls makes them stop."
items.answer: Trolls want attention, so they should be ignored.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Trolls want attention, so they should be ignored.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Fatima submitted an essay copied from a website as her own work without giving credit. Which violation of intellectual property is this?
items.answer: Plagiarism
items.markingKey: (a) This is plagiarism.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about digital footprints and etiquettes is NOT correct?
items.answer: Only data posted by a user forms the digital footprint.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. Passive data such as IP address and browsing history also form it.
options: Only data posted by a user forms the digital footprint.
Communication etiquette asks us to be precise, polite and credible.
A digital footprint can be used to trace a person's online activities.
Respecting others' privacy and diversity is part of net etiquette.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Creators release work under Creative Commons licences.
Reason (R): Everything available on the Internet is free to copy and use.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Most online content is protected by copyright unless its licence allows reuse.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Riya found that all the files on his laptop were encrypted and a message demanded payment in cryptocurrency to unlock them.
(i) Identify the cyber crime. (1)
(ii) Suggest two ways to protect oneself from it. (2)
(iii) Name the Indian law that deals with cyber crimes. (1)
items.answer:
(i) Ransomware.
(ii) Keep regular offline backups; update the operating system and antivirus; do not open unknown attachments.
(iii) The Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act), amended in 2008.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) 1, (ii) 1 each for two measures, (iii) 1.

items.stem: Which principle of e-waste management is followed by donating a working old laptop to a school?
items.answer: Reuse
items.markingKey: (a) This is reuse.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about data protection, intellectual property rights and licensing:
I. Copyright exists automatically once a work is created.
II. Everything available on the Internet is free to copy and use.
III. Giving credit makes copying a whole copyrighted work legal.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is incorrect: Most online content is protected by copyright unless its licence allows reuse. III is incorrect: Credit avoids plagiarism but permission or a suitable licence is still needed.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Secretly listening to or intercepting private communication on a network.
items.answer: eavesdropping
items.markingKey: (c) eavesdropping: secretly listening to or intercepting private communication on a network.

items.stem: What is FOSS? Give two examples.
items.answer: Free and Open Source Software: software whose source code is freely available to use, modify and share. Examples: Linux, LibreOffice, Mozilla Firefox, Python, GIMP.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for each correct point.

items.stem: What is meant by 'net etiquette' in the context of digital footprints and etiquettes?
items.answer: The code of good behaviour to be followed while using the Internet.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: net etiquette correctly explained as the code of good behaviour to be followed while using the Internet.

items.stem: The following statement about data protection, intellectual property rights and licensing is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "A patent protects the logo of a company."
items.answer: A trademark protects a logo; a patent protects an invention.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (A trademark protects a logo; a patent protects an invention.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Zoya's school is replacing 26 old computers, printers and UPS batteries.
(i) What is this discarded equipment called? (1)
(ii) Give one harmful effect of throwing it in a landfill. (1)
(iii) Suggest two ways the school can manage it responsibly. (2)
items.answer:
(i) E-waste (electronic waste).
(ii) Toxic substances such as lead, mercury and cadmium leak into soil and groundwater (or burning releases toxic fumes).
(iii) Donate working computers (reuse); give the rest to an authorised e-waste recycler (recycle); return batteries through take-back schemes.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) 1, (ii) 1, (iii) 1 each for two ways.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about digital footprints and etiquettes is correct?
items.answer: Respecting others' privacy and diversity is part of net etiquette.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Copies may remain with others and on servers, so footprints are hard to erase. Trolls want attention, so they should be ignored. Passive data such as IP address and browsing history also form it.
options: Only data posted by a user forms the digital footprint.
Respecting others' privacy and diversity is part of net etiquette.
Replying angrily to trolls makes them stop.
Deleting a post removes every copy of it from the Internet.

items.stem: The following statement about open source software, cyber crimes and cyber laws is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Free software always means software with no cost and no source code."
items.answer: Free refers to freedom to use, study, modify and share the source code.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Free refers to freedom to use, study, modify and share the source code.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: What is e-waste? Give two of its harmful effects.
items.answer: Discarded electronic devices such as phones, computers and batteries. Effects: toxic metals (lead, mercury, cadmium) pollute soil and water; burning releases harmful fumes; health problems for workers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for each correct point.

items.stem: The following statement about e-waste management and health concerns is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Recycling means buying fewer gadgets."
items.answer: That is reducing; recycling recovers materials from old devices.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (That is reducing; recycling recovers materials from old devices.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Ransomware often spreads through e-mail attachments and infected downloads. The IT Act gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures. FOSS can be modified and redistributed by users. Linux, Python and Mozilla Firefox are examples of open source software."
(i) Explain the term 'proprietary software', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Public Wi-Fi is risky for online banking. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Ethical hacking is a crime." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) Software owned by a company whose source code is not shared and which is used under a paid licence. (ii) Data on unsecured networks can be intercepted by eavesdroppers. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Ethical hacking is authorised testing to improve security.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Software owned by a company whose source code is not shared and which is used under a paid licence. (ii) Data on unsecured networks can be intercepted by eavesdroppers. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Ethical hacking is authorised testing to improve security.
